title: The Collector's Vault
subtitle: Data Wrangling Assignment · group_by + summarise
story: You are a forest ecologist on an alien world — and, if you’re honest, a collector first. Your days are spent high in the canopy, riding the monorail between research stations, measuring impossibly tall trees and cataloguing what you find. But every evening ends the same way: the long climb to the cliff, and the sealed alien gate you have never once managed to open. They say a true artifact waits inside. Today you’ll make your rounds one more time — and try the vault again. Golden morning mist still hangs in the crowns as you reach the first station, deep in the canopy, where your instrument is already humming with fresh measurements.

done.title: The way is clear!
done.body: You read the grove census the careful way, and the boulder rolls aside. Golden hour spills over the last stretch of trail — the cliff, and the vault, are just ahead.

escapeDone.title: The vault opens!
escapeDone.body: Three shapes, three groupings — you matched every line’s collection to how it was sorted, and the ancient gate finally swings wide. Inside, at last, the artifact. It’s yours. The mist lifts over the canopy as the sun goes down.

musicCredit.text: Yuuf - In The Sun (Live in Surrey Hills)

coverPrompt: Minimalist stylised thumbnail poster of a lone alien cliff-side vault gate glowing with a single warm amber light at sunset, set into a rocky mountain precipice above an endless sea of misty tree canopy. Designed to read clearly as a small thumbnail: one bold, simple, high-contrast silhouette, iconic and uncluttered, minimal fine detail. Flat, limited palette: deep teal, icy blue, and one warm amber glow. Soft film grain, painterly but clean with simple geometric shapes. Strong negative space, single centred focal subject. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos. Square composition.

entry.title: The climb
entry.text: Instruments packed, the day’s rounds done. The triangle car leaves the trees behind and sets you on a ledge high on the mountain — and a boulder blocks the cleft. Golden hour, the peaks close now. One more attempt at the vault, if you can clear the way.

rooms.designNote: BOSS — THE REGROUP (puzzleType 2, isBoss, deliverable figure+codec). Re-asks S3's zone question the CAREFUL way; the engineered Simpson flip makes the answer a DIFFERENT grove. TASK: group_by(canopy_zone, species) |> summarise(m = mean(vitality_index)); ungroup; group_by(canopy_zone) |> summarise(mean(m)); bar chart. ANSWER: Sunspire Heights (64.2 species-balanced; Cragside 58.5). PROMPT (draft): 'The vault won’t answer to a careless count. Not where the strong trees happen to stand, but which GROUND truly grows a tree best — giving every kind of tree an equal say. Which grove is the finest ground to grow in?' OPTIONS (>=6): Sunspire Heights[correct], Cragside (THE SHORTCUT TRAP — must be present), Mistfen Reach, Hollowdeep + 2 (e.g. 'No real difference'; Bloomspire = grouped by species by mistake). CLUE (draft field note): 'Rank the groves by the vigour of the trees standing in them and Cragside always wins. But Cragside is thick with Bloomspire and Ironcrown — hardy stock that reads strong wherever it roots. That tells me the grove is full of strong trees, not that it grows them strong. To judge the ground itself I must give every kind of tree an equal say — take each species’ vigour grove by grove first, then compare the groves.' feedback.correct NAMES the answer (field-notebook / meta): 'Sunspire Heights is the true best ground.' ART: HIGH on the mountain, golden hour; BOULDER blocks the way; console on a rock; pinned note; canopy far below, peaks close; open passage back down.

rooms.title: The cliff-top vault

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a panorama. A 360-degree view from a windswept mountain cliff-top at sunset — the highest point of the whole journey — the rock and sky wrapping continuously around so the left and right edges meet seamlessly. Ahead, an ancient alien GATE set into a sheer rock face — a sealed vault door of dark stone and softly glowing amber inlay. Beside it, set into the rock, a panel bearing a blank 3-by-3 grid of recessed buttons. All around, the mist has finally LIFTED to reveal a breathtaking clear vista: an endless valley of tree canopy glowing in the sunset far below and a whole ridge of mountain peaks standing clear across the horizon. Behind, an OPEN trail leading back down the scramble. Warm sunset gold and rose against deep teal shadow, one bright amber glow at the gate, drifting spores. painterly, cinematic, cheerful and hopeful, warm golden light with soft teal shadows in the mist, gentle bioluminescent amber lichen-glow, drifting spores, subtle film grain. No people, no lettering, no text, no captions, no UI.

entry.title: The cliff-top
entry.text: The boulder is behind you. You crest the scramble to the highest point of all as the sun touches the horizon and the mist finally lifts — the whole canopy and every peak ablaze in gold. And there it is: the gate you’ve never opened, and beside it a panel of nine blank buttons.

plannedHotspots.label: The vault gate panel
plannedHotspots.note: NEW 'grid-select' puzzle type (3x3): COLUMNS = the three car shapes (square/circle/triangle), ROWS = the three traits (colour/size/shape). Pick, per column, the trait that line's collection was sorted by. Beetles=colour, cones=size, shells=shape. Ungraded escape gate (out of codec).

plannedHotspots.label: The trail back down
plannedHotspots.note: return to the boss ledge (and on down the cars to re-inspect the collections)

rooms.designNote: VAULT / ESCAPE (ungraded, no codec). The 3x3 grid gate: COLUMNS keyed by DOOR SHAPE (square / circle / triangle), ROWS the three traits (COLOUR / SIZE / SHAPE). Correct mapping: square=COLOUR (beetles), circle=SIZE (cones), triangle=SHAPE (shells). One selection per column; correct vector fires solveRoom -> escapeDone. NO notebook pickups (Lucas: force backtracking) — the player must remember, or ride back DOWN through the cars to re-read the trays (the framed collector's notes flagged each on the way up). => the single-door shared-node BACK-NAV is load-bearing here. NEW ENGINE WORK: build the 'grid-select' puzzle type (sibling of lock/ledger; see notes/puzzle_inventory.md) and the ride-beat. ART: HIGHEST point, sunset cliff-top, mist LIFTED to a full canopy+peaks vista, the alien gate + a blank 3x3 button panel; artifact revealed on solve. PLAYTEST WATCH: with forced backtracking + single-door cars, re-inspecting from the vault is a long ride down-and-up — the framed notes must make each collection memorable enough that most players don't need the trek.
